reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Reversing the direction (higher FUNC is better).
name: FUNC Score

version.label: FUNC (Rost et al. 2008)
version.detail: Five components, 0–11. Higher scores were associated with a greater likelihood of 90-day functional independence (GOS ≥4).

purpose: Estimates the likelihood of functional independence at 90 days after primary ICH.
intendedPopulation: Adults with primary intracerebral haemorrhage, assessed at diagnosis.

calculatorNotice.title: Group-level estimate
calculatorNotice.message: Higher scores mean better expected function. Goals-of-care decisions should not rest on the FUNC score alone.

resultStates.label: FUNC 0–4
resultStates.summary: No patient with FUNC ≤4 achieved 90-day functional independence in the derivation cohort.
resultStates.detail: Group-level finding; integrate with the full clinical picture and avoid early care limitation based on the score alone.

resultStates.label: FUNC {total}
resultStates.summary: The likelihood of 90-day functional independence increased with the score in the derivation cohort.

resultStates.label: FUNC 11
resultStates.summary: FUNC 11 at this assessment: over 80% achieved 90-day functional independence in the derivation cohort.

clinicalContext.text: Complements severity grading (ICH Score) with an estimate of functional outcome.

clinicalInsights.text: Use at diagnosis, not as a repeatedly changing measure.
Pre-ICH cognitive impairment is assessed from history, often with an informant.

limitations.text: Derived and validated at a single institution.

limitations: Excludes traumatic ICH and haemorrhage from other causes.
Outcome defined by GOS ≥4 at 90 days.

confounders.effect: ABC/2 error affects the volume band.

guideSections.what: A 0–11 score estimating likelihood of 90-day functional independence after primary ICH.
guideSections.whenToUse: When primary ICH is first identified.
guideSections.howToPerform: Score volume, age, location, GCS and pre-ICH cognitive status; sum.
guideSections.clinicalContext: A group-level estimate for discussion, alongside the full clinical picture.

sources.citation: Rost NS, Smith EE, Chang Y, et al. Prediction of functional outcome in patients with primary intracerebral hemorrhage: the FUNC score. Stroke. 2008;39(8):2304-2309.
